points.description: States that the height of a tree is the length of the longest path from the root down to a leaf (i.e., the maximum number of edges/levels from root to the deepest leaf), in any wording.
points.partial_credit: Award about 2-3 marks if the answer gives only part of the idea, e.g. 'distance from the root to a leaf' or 'number of levels' without saying longest/deepest.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying the height is the longest path (or depth/number of levels) from the root to the deepest leaf, however briefly or informally worded. Part marks for vague or incomplete answers, such as a root-to-leaf distance with no mention of longest, or just the number of levels. No marks for unrelated ideas such as the number of nodes or the number of children. Extra remarks do not cost marks unless they contradict the core idea.
